Key audit matter:
The fair value of investment properties is
determined based on the most appropriate
methodology applicable to the specific property.
Methodologies include the market comparable
approach that reflects recent transaction prices
for similar properties, discounted cash flows and
income capitalisation methodologies.
How our audit addressed the Key audit ma:
⎯ assessing the accuracy of the projected
rental income and projected expenses
(related costs) used in the valuation model
to supporting lease contracts and historical
expenditure patterns based on prior year
actual costs and the projected inflationary
adjustments to costs.

Key audit matter:
The valuation process, under the income
approach, involves significant estimates and
assumptions of unobservable inputs in the
valuation models such as projected future cash
flows, future rent escalations, exit values and the
discount rates.
The fair values of the investment properties are
highly sensitive to the changes in the underlying
estimates and assumptions.
We have therefore identified the valuation of
investment property using the income approach
as a key audit matter due to the materiality of the
carrying amount and the significant judgement
underlying the valuation.
How our audit addressed the Key audit ma:
⎯ Challenged the appropriateness of the
discount rate and terminal yield rates used
in the valuation by comparing the discount
rate to market rates and terminal yield to
available industry data, taking into
consideration comparability to houses
indices and market factors.
Evaluating the adequacy of financial
statements disclosures, including disclosures
of key judgements and assumptions used in
determining fair values in accordance with the
requirements of IFRS 13 Fair Value
Measurements.
